card.title: npx launchreel build examples/self --offline
card.subtitle: No API key. No network. No Python. MIT.

narration.text: You shipped something. You need a video about it, and a day is the last thing you want to spend on one.
Every demo-video tool on the market records your clicks. None of them understand what happened.
But developers already produce a perfect record of what their software does: a terminal session.
LaunchReel reads that session, works out what was actually demonstrated, and builds the video around that.
One part is genuinely hard. Generated music cannot be told to put an accent at fourteen seconds.
So LaunchReel generates several candidates, measures every one with librosa, and moves the cuts onto the beats it actually finds.
The first version asked for a single brief and got a track whose first beat landed at eleven seconds. No amount of snapping saves a cut at four in a track like that.
Narration works the same way. Every line is synthesized and measured before the timeline is fixed.
When a line overruns, the shot stretches. When it cannot, the line goes back with a character budget.
You get two things, not one. An mp4 — and an OTIO file, the timeline itself.
It opens in a real editor with every shot as its own clip, narration and music on separate tracks, and the cut points marked where the beats are.
No other tool in this space gives you the project file. You get an mp4 and a shrug.
It ships with a recorded session, so the first run needs no API key, no network, no Python. Free and open source. MIT.
